text:
Akshay: starting a thread to lock down a "golden run" protocol for quantized benchmarks — we keep getting noisy FLOPS vs quality tradeoffs. want a short checklist we can run reliably.
Maria: yes please. main pain points?
Akshay: kernel selection differences (fp8 vs int8 vs 4-bit), calibration routines, warmup, power/clock limits on nodes, tokenization differences.
Jenna: + batching heuristics and KV-cache priming. small batch vs microbatch ordering flips perf numbers.
Kevin: propose a baseline: same seed, same tokenizer, single pinned model sha, 3 warmup lengths (0, 16, 64 tokens), and report median of 5 runs. keep power limit at 100W and also run at unlocked for one comparison.
Akshay: agree. Also force same kernel selection policy: e.g., prefer INT8 kernels for matmuls if the runtime reports accuracy within threshold; otherwise fall back to FP16. need a deterministic kernel chooser flag.
Maria: can we add config snippet for the runner? putting it here to copy into jobs:
```json
{
  "model_pin": "sha256:abc123",
  "kernel_policy": "deterministic-prefer-int8",
  "calibration": "per-layer-static",
  "warmup_tokens": 16,
  "batching": {
    "max_batch": 8,
    "microbatch_size": 1,
    "flush_after": 50
  },
  "power_limit_watts": 100
}
```
Jenna: for KV cache we should always run long context prefix priming: run a 512-token prefix to populate caches, then measure next-n tokens. otherwise model cold-start dominates.
Kevin: agree, add a 'kv_priming_tokens' param. Also record first-token latency separately.
Akshay: about calibration: run both per-layer static and per-channel dynamic where supported. measure perplexity/regression on a fixed eval set (we'll use the same 200 prompts). log calibration stats and quantization ranges.
Maria: note on tokenization: some tokenizers (esp old sentencepiece) can produce different average token lengths across versions. we should vendor the tokenizer binary and hash it in the run metadata.
Jenna: perf-bot finished a run earlier, attaching summary: 
perf-bot: run 1792109800 finished. model=rw-7b-quant int8; median latency=32.4ms; p95=85ms; quality delta=+0.2 ppl; calibration=per-layer-static; warmup=16; kv_primed=512. artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/1792109800/
Kevin: good. action items: 1) add deterministic kernel flag to runtime (Akshay), 2) update bench harness to vendor tokenizer (Maria), 3) add kv_priming param (Jenna), 4) create bench dashboard that shows warmup impact (Kevin).
Akshay: I'll open a tiny PR for kernel flag and a separate RFC for the protocol doc.
Maria: I'll add the tokenizer vendoring and include token counts in run CSV.
Jenna: I'll implement kv priming and add a histogram of first-token vs steady-state latencies.
Kevin: let's aim to run the new protocol on next week's quant-ci slot. tagging @here in the channel to FYI. :rocket:
Akshay: thanks, team. we'll try to keep runs <2h each and attach raw profiles (nvprof / nsight) to the artifacts.
Maria: one more: include the full runtime config dump with kernel selection trace for each run so we can repro which kernels were chosen for each op.
Akshay: +1. that will help root cause perf regressions vs quant changes.
perf-bot: benchmark-agent: scheduled job 1792110500 for next-week slot.
